thread:
Maria: Heads-up — after enabling FP8 on H100 (L40S images) for the small-canary pool we saw a ~2.3x tail-latency spike on chat workloads between 14:02-14:05 UTC. Numbers: p50 ~18ms (expected), p95 jumped from 120ms -> 280ms, p99 -> 740ms. Logs show a burst of kernel handoffs + repeated kv-cache miss churn.

Ajay: Oof. Any repro traces? stack / perf counters?

Maria: Attached quick profiling snippet from tracer:
```
SM% utilization drops to 12% for ~30-80ms windows during context switch
CUDA streams blocked on mutex: transformer_kernel_selector::choose_kernel()
KV cache miss rate spikes from 4% -> 22% concurrently
Counts of fallback_kernels executed: FP8_fastpath: 386 -> falling back to INT8_slowpath: 1420
```

Zach: Interesting. That looks like a synchronization stall when switching kernels mid-batch. Could be our selector acquiring a global lock while probing compatibility with transformer-engine kernels.

Eva: Also see this in the telemetry: those same hosts show sudden tensor core underutilization and more host->device memcpy calls, which matches kernel fallback/backfill. Might be kernel binary not preloaded for some model shapes so first invocations do JIT/compile.

Ajay: Two hypotheses: 1) kernel selection acquires a global scheduler lock causing stream serialization during batch boundary when FP8 path fails and falls back; 2) KV hot cache eviction policy interacting with microbatching causes spikes in miss-rate which then forces different execution path (wider sequence -> switch kernels).

Maria: Repro script I ran (small-loop):
```
for i in $(seq 1 200); do
  curl -sS -X POST $CANARY_ENDPOINT -d @payload.json
  sleep 0.05
done
```
Payload is 1-2 tokens warm prefix then 800 token decode. Tail latency spike reproducible in ~20% of runs.

Zach: Can you dump kernel selector traces with DEBUG=1? Specifically log: chosen_kernel, reason, fallback_reason, selector_lock_wait_us. If lock wait > 100us often we have bad hotspot.

Maria: Uploaded debug log excerpt: selector_lock_wait_us median=12us but 95th=820us; many entries with fallback_reason="quant-profile-mismatch" and "kernel-not-loaded".

Ajay: That points to two actionable things: 1) avoid global lock by doing lock-free read path + background kernel probe; 2) pre-warm kernel binaries & place per-GPU kernel cache to reduce kernel-not-loaded path. Also investigate KV policy: if kv miss bursts correlate with worker reclaim/evict we should raise hot-cache threshold for FP8 runs.

Eva: Agreed. I also recommend adaptive microbatch sizing: if KV hit-rate < 10% then reduce microbatch to avoid creating longer sequences that trigger different kernel selection. We can add a dynamic heuristic: batch_size = base * min(1, 0.8 + 0.2 * kv_hit_rate).

Maria: Proposed short-term mitigations for canary: revert FP8 kernel for models with >256 seq or pin FP8 only for shorter sequences; increase kernel pre-warm concurrency during rollout; bump kv hot threshold from 0.6 -> 0.8 for the affected pool.

Ajay: I'll prototype a lock-free fast-check: check an atomic pointer to currently preferred_kernel, if failure then queue an async probe task instead of blocking the serving thread. If probe fails later we can gracefully fallback without blocking.

Zach: I can add telemetry hooks: emit events when kernel switch happens with tags (model, seq_len, kv_hit_rate, host_temp, kernel_load_time_us). That'll help correlate.

infra-bot: canary-deploy: fp8-h100-l40s-canary v12 rolled to 8 nodes at 14:00 UTC :rocket:

Maria: After applying pre-warm script (loading fp8 kernels at start) the p95 dropped back to ~140ms but p99 still ~300ms. So partial improvement.

Ajay: Good. Next steps: I'll land the async-probe change behind a flag and run paired comparison. Zach — hook in the telemetry. Eva — run a kv-policy sweep to find sweet spot that avoids eviction churn. Maria — keep canary on and pause wider rollout until p99 < 200ms for 1 hour.

Maria: timeline — plan to test async-probe flag tonight at 02:00 PST. If green, progressive rollout tomorrow morning. Will post results here. :thumbsup:

Zach: One more note — check transformer-engine config flags for L40S vs H100. We might be linking different kernel variants across images causing kernel-not-loaded. I saw mismatch in /etc/transformer-engine.conf on two hosts.

Eva: Logged an infra task: INFRA-1296 to sync TE packages across pools.

Maria: Thanks team. If anyone is free after the 02:00 run ping me and we'll sweep logs together.

Ajay: Will do.
